summary.headline: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 52% YoY to INR4,314 million and EBITDA hit a record INR1,020 million, with margin at 23.6%.
summary.overview: Revenue grew 52% YoY and 10% QoQ to a record INR4,314 million, with H1 revenue at INR8,241 million. EBITDA rose 50% YoY to INR1,020 million, margin 23.6%, or 28% excluding ramp-up losses at New Delhi and Faridabad Sector-20. PAT was INR485 million for Q2 (+17% YoY) and INR939 million for H1. The company signed a strategic partnership with Advent International for INR3,150 crore primary capital, awaiting CCI approval, with the first INR1,750 crore tranche expected after approval.

financial_highlights.change: Adjusted 28% excluding New Delhi and Faridabad Sector-20 ramp-up losses

segments.name: Existing hospitals (Noida, Greater Noida, Noida Extension, Jhansi-Orchha)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR3,109 million, +24% YoY; inpatient volumes +28%; occupancy 78% vs 71% a year ago; EBITDA margin above 28%.

segments.name: Newer hospitals (Greater Faridabad, New Delhi, Faridabad Sector-20, Agra)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR1,205 million, 28% of group revenue vs 11% a year ago; collectively moved from EBITDA loss to positive EBITDA in H1. Greater Faridabad occupancy 77%.

segments.name: New Delhi (Model Town)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue about INR26 crore, ARPOB about INR50,000; loss narrowed to INR38 million from INR55 million in Q1; management guides December as break-even month.

segments.name: Faridabad Sector-20
segments.commentary: Turned EBITDA positive; Q2 revenue about INR40 crore; over 80% of business from cash and private insurance; ARPOB about INR40,000.

segments.name: Agra
segments.commentary: EBITDA positive in Q2 on revenue of about INR20 crore; ARPOB INR33,000; occupancy 58%.

guidance_outlook: Company-level EBITDA margin guidance of about 24% and above maintained for coming quarters and years, despite oncology price cap impact.
Oncology drug margin cap at 30% estimated to reduce EBITDA by about 0.3%; management plans to offset through operational efficiencies.
Existing organic plan of 30% YoY revenue growth for next 3-4 years; organic bed target of 5,000 beds in 3-4 years unchanged.
Advent funds to add about 2,000-3,000 beds via acquisitions in about four years; 40-50% of these beds may go live from next financial year.
Target of 7,000-8,000 total beds over 3-5 years; management says EBITDA could exceed 3x current levels in 3.5-4 years.
Gurugram Sector 40 (250 beds, ARPOB above INR50,000) expected to operationalize next financial year; break-even targeted in about 15 months.
Model Town (Delhi) expected to break even in December 2026 / H2 FY27.
Government business mix expected to fall toward 20% target; current payer mix about 34% government, down from 37% last quarter.
Collections in H1 seasonally lower; full-year EBITDA to CFO conversion expected at 70% or above.
capex_capacity: Current operational beds about 2,800 (up from 1,405 at listing in August 2023); about 350-400 beds yet to be operationalized across Faridabad, Model Town and Agra, expected within 2-3 quarters.

Faridabad Sector-20 oncology: equipment installed; AERB clearances pending; medical and surgical oncology live, full spectrum including radiation and nuclear expected in next 45-60 days and two months respectively.
Model Town radiation oncology requires new bunker setup; construction on hold due to GRAP 2; timeline about 8-9 months.
Agra: CTVS and cardiac surgery recently added; paediatric cardiac planned; renovation and additional beds planned.
Gurugram: revamping existing building and adding capacity; construction on remaining part to start after plan approval.
No brownfield expansion planned for Noida, Greater Noida and Jhansi; Advent money not for greenfield, targeting fully owned, EBITDA-positive running assets.
Debt rose on Gurugram (about INR100 crore) and medical equipment (about INR100 crore or more); management calls current debt the peak level.
demand_pricing: Group ARPOB INR36,000, up 11% YoY; Noida Extension about INR51,000, Delhi about INR47,000, Greater Noida INR43,000, Noida INR37,000, New Faridabad INR37,000, Greater Faridabad INR33,000, Agra INR33,000, Jhansi about INR14,000.
Payer mix: government about 34% (37% prior quarter); remainder split roughly equally between private insurance and cash, with private insurance a few points higher; international about 4-5%.

International business grew over 35% from H2 FY26 to H1 FY27 but remains single-digit share; affected in recent months by war and Gulf situation; partnerships in CIS, Africa, Mauritius, Ethiopia, South Sudan.
Oncology: capped margin of 30% on a list of cancer drugs; management says impact about 0.3% of EBITDA. Management sees no impact on oncology volumes in Greater Noida.
Management noted possible further drug pricing regulation after a Supreme Court matter; no decision yet, industry has made representations.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of cancer drug price capping on top line and bottom line?
qa_highlights.answer: Estimated reduction of about 0.3% in EBITDA from the 30% margin cap on listed oncology drugs; group EBITDA guidance of about 24% unchanged, offset via efficiencies.

qa_highlights.question: Timing of Advent deal and tranche structure?
qa_highlights.answer: CCI approval at final stage, expected this month after Diwali. INR3,150 crore in two tranches: INR1,750 crore after CCI approval, balance after 15-18 months subject to conditions.

qa_highlights.question: Expansion strategy and asset type for Advent capital?
qa_highlights.answer: Focus on multi-specialty hospitals, chains in North India prioritized, open to other regions; acquisitions to be EBITDA positive and mostly 100% equity-owned; around 2,000-3,000 beds to be added in about four years on top of the 5,000-bed organic plan.

qa_highlights.question: Oncology status at Faridabad and Model Town, and Model Town break-even?
qa_highlights.answer: Faridabad Sector-20 full oncology in 45-60 days, radiation in two months. Model Town radiation about 8-9 months away. Model Town loss reduced to INR38 million from INR55 million in Q1; December expected as break-even month.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the gross debt rising and what is the peak?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt increase driven by about INR100 crore for Gurugram and over INR100 crore for medical equipment; management says this is the peak level for the next few quarters, with marginal reduction possible.

qa_highlights.question: Gurugram breakeven and margin outlook given new assets?
qa_highlights.answer: Gurugram break-even targeted in 15 months, described as conservative; EBITDA margins expected to stay above 24% and on a rising trend, blended margin depends on deals.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for FY28-FY29 P&L contribution from Advent deployment?
qa_highlights.answer: Existing 30% organic revenue growth visible for 3-4 years; Advent capital expected to add EBITDA on top, with management suggesting EBITDA could pass 3x current levels in 3.5-4 years.

risks_watch: Oncology drug margin cap and possible extension of price caps to other drugs (Supreme Court matter pending).
Advent deal completion depends on CCI and other regulatory approvals; second tranche of INR1,400 crore-equivalent balance tied to conditions after 15-18 months.
Collections seasonality: EBITDA to CFO conversion softened in H1; needs to recover to 70% or above by year-end.
Income tax (IT) matter: final demand received, company appealing; management expects demand to reduce.
Agra occupancy fell sharply QoQ while ARPOB rose; management says mix is being optimized and ramp continues.
Gurugram ramp, Model Town break-even and Agra specialty changes are execution items to track next quarter.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on growth, Advent partnership and near-term profitability of new hospitals; more guarded and deflecting on regulatory matters (drug pricing, IT demand) and on the detailed timeline and returns for Advent-funded acquisitions.
key_quotes: Quarter 2 FY27 was the strongest quarter to date, with revenue growth of 52% year-on-year and EBITDA growth of 50%.
Our overall group level EBITDA will not change going forward because of this policy.
The assets that we will continue to acquire from this fund will always be EBITDA positive hospitals.
We feel that this is the peak level of debt for us, at least for the next few quarters to come.

About 350-400 beds yet to be operationalized across Faridabad, Model Town and Agra
Gurugram Sector 40 hospital (250 beds, ARPOB above INR50,000)

growth.why: Management guides 30% YoY organic revenue growth for 3-4 years, a 5,000-bed organic target, and 7,000-8,000 total beds with Advent-funded 2,000-3,000 acquired beds; delivery is backed by about 350-400 beds due in 2-3 quarters and Gurugram 250 beds next FY, but Advent beds and the 5,000-bed target lack dated contracts or orders, so backing is partial.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Company-level EBITDA margin guided at about 24%+ and held; Q2 margin 23.6% (28% excluding New Delhi and Faridabad Sector-20 ramp-up losses), with Model Town break-even in December and Gurugram targeted at 15 months, offset by about 0.3% EBITDA hit from the 30% oncology margin cap.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: About 350-400 beds (~13% of 2,800 operational) are under construction across Faridabad, Model Town and Agra due in 2-3 quarters, and Gurugram Sector 40 (250 beds) is expected next financial year; Advent-funded acquisitions add 40-50% of 2,000-3,000 beds from next FY.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides about 30% YoY organic revenue growth for 3-4 years; Q2 revenue +52% YoY, existing hospitals' inpatient volumes +28% and occupancy 72% group (78% at existing hospitals), with 350-400 beds still to be operationalized.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Group occupancy at 72% with no brownfield expansion planned at Noida, Greater Noida or Jhansi, so growth depends on new hospitals and Advent-funded acquisitions (INR3,150 crore, CCI approval expected after Diwali) that will need announcements.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA +50% YoY and H1 revenue +52% YoY ran ahead, but management kept the 24% margin and 30% growth guidance rather than raising it, and oncology price caps are a headwind.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Margin guidance of about 24%+ held despite the oncology cap (about 0.3% EBITDA impact) and Q2 margin was 23.6% with 28% ex-ramp-up losses; risks are more about further drug-pricing regulation and collections (EBITDA to CFO needs 70%+).

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Faridabad Sector-20 full oncology (medical and surgical live, radiation in 45-60 days, nuclear in about two months) and Agra paediatric cardiac planned; Model Town radiation oncology 8-9 months away.

rows.label: Advent INR3,150 crore primary capital and acquisitions
rows.when: CCI approval after Diwali; first INR1,750 crore tranche then
rows.why: Deal at final CCI stage; INR1,750 crore after approval and balance after 15-18 months funds about 2,000-3,000 acquired beds in about four years.

rows.label: Gross debt peaking; net debt INR392 million vs cash INR4,289 million
rows.why: Debt rose on Gurugram (about INR100 crore) and equipment (over INR100 crore), management calls this the peak with marginal reduction possible; cash of INR4,289 million covers net debt.

rows.label: Collections recovery to 70%+ EBITDA-to-CFO
rows.why: H1 collections seasonally weak; management guides full-year EBITDA to CFO at 70% or above versus H1 operating cash flow of INR1,113 million (+49% YoY).

tone.note: Management was confident on growth, the Advent partnership and near-term profitability of new hospitals (Model Town break-even in December, Gurugram in 15 months), but deflected on drug-pricing regulation, the IT demand and the timing and returns of Advent-funded acquisitions; analysts probed margin
